cards.text: This one's a song for the choirmaster, played on stringed instruments. The singers keep saying "us," and they open with a big ask. They pray, "May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us".

cards.question: True or false: when the singers ask God to make His face shine on them, they're asking Him to look on them with kindness.

cards.text: After a Selah, the singers say WHY they want all that blessing. Me, fresh out of the junk drawer? I'd have asked for a bigger oven and a REALLY long nap.

cards.question: Why do the singers want God to bless them?

answers.text: So His ways are known on earth
So their land is safe from war
So they can rest from hard work

cards.question: True or false: the singers want God's salvation known only among their own people.

cards.text: Then the song breaks into a chorus, and it calls on somebody to praise God. I LOVE a chorus, friend, because it's the only part of any song I can actually remember.

cards.question: The chorus calls on someone to praise God. Who?

cards.text: Next they say, "Let the nations be glad and sing for joy," and they give a reason. Joy for EVERY nation, friend, and I get excited when a batch comes out not burnt.

cards.question: Why should the nations be glad and sing for joy?

cards.text: He judges the peoples justly, and He leads the nations of the earth. After another Selah, the chorus comes right back word for word, and I'd sing it twice too, but trust me, NOBODY wants to hear me sing it twice.
Then the song stops asking and points at the land itself.

cards.question: The song points at the land. What does it say the earth has given?
True or false: the song opened asking God to bless the singers, and now they say God, their God, blesses them.

cards.text: One last line, and the blessing shows up one more time. And then, friend, the singers say what it's for.

cards.question: God blesses the singers so that who will fear Him?

answers.text: All the ends of the earth

findings.problem: The setup joke says Papa Dorin would have asked for 'a REALLY long nap,' and frames this as the opposite of what the singers asked for. That points the baker away from the wrong answer 'So they can rest from hard work' on card 4.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only the priests', 'Only the singers'), and the right answer 'All the peoples' doesn't. Card 5 had just taught that the 'only' option is false, so the right answer stands out by its form.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card is one bare sentence ('Then the song stops asking and points at the land itself.'). It has none of Papa Dorin's voice and only a thin setup for the turn to the harvest.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
